question: An uncodified constitution cannot contain written legal documents. Explain whether the United Kingdom example supports this claim.

draft.raw: O1|P2.2,P3.2|United Kingdom|2026-10-01|The United Kingdom's constitution is an example of an uncodified constitution, which is not contained in a single document but is instead composed of multiple sources including fundamental acts, court cases, and treaties, thus contradicting the claim that an uncodified constitution cannot contain written legal documents.

claims.subject: United Kingdom
claims.text: The United Kingdom's constitution is an example of an uncodified constitution, which is not contained in a single document but is instead composed of multiple sources including fundamental acts, court cases, and treaties, thus contradicting the claim that an uncodified constitution cannot contain written legal documents.

references.label: P2.2
references.text: The constitution of the United Kingdom is a notable example of an uncodified constitution; it is instead written in numerous fundamental acts of a legislature, court cases, and treaties.[2]

references.label: P3.2
references.text: A treaty that establishes an international organization is also its constitution, in that it would define how that organization is constituted.
